newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ dollar heads firm into RBNZ statement.
newsitem.headline: NZ dollar heads firm into RBNZ statement.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar closed slightly firmer on Wednesday heading into the Reserve Bank's economic projections.
The Kiwi finished at US$0.7053/60 and 69.12 on its Trade-Weighted Index, from 0.7045/52 and 69.00 at the opening.
"The market's getting itself long in anticipation of a further worsening inflation track and, implicit in that, a relatively hawkish sort of a statement," one dealer said.

He said the market was following a familiar pattern of buying the currency heading into a Reserve Bank statement. The economic forecasts are due for release at 9 a.m. on Thursday (2000 GMT Wednesday).
Another dealer agreed that past form suggested the bank would deliver a hawkish, hold-the-line message.
He said the currency was drawing strength from some local corporate buying, a stronger Australian dollar and the continuation of Tuesday's short squeeze ahead of the release.
The statement will be the first to take account of an extra NZ$5 billion of government spending planned over three years by the centre-right coalition which took office in December.
The market saw little new in comments by Treasurer Winston Peters to parliament's finance and expenditure committee, where he said he did not expect RBNZ Governor Don Brash to go soft on inflation.
Peters said the widening of the bank's target band for underlying inflation to 0-3 percent from 0-2 percent had slowed down the rise of the Kiwi dollar.
